references.text: The same basket (תֵּבָה) that was placed in the reeds by the Nile's bank is now found by Pharaoh's daughter.
Pharaoh's command to throw all Hebrew baby boys into the Nile stands in contrast to his own daughter now saving a child from that very river.
Pharaoh's daughter later adopts the child she found by the river and gives him the name Moses.
The Hebrew word תֵּבָה (ark/basket) is used only here and for Noah's ark, both as rescue vessels on water.
Stephen refers to this event in his speech, where he says that Pharaoh's daughter took up Moses and raised him as her own son.
The book of Hebrews mentions that Moses, when he became an adult, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, referring back to this rescue.
